subject: Argus security follow-up: annotated edge-anchored isolation model for Dedicated + Private
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@argusfin.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Argus Security Team <security@argusfin.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: need isolation proof for Dedicated + Private deployments

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The security team asked us for a compact, annotated diagram that highlights the controls and enforcement points between customer workloads and Redwood control-plane for both Dedicated and Private deployment options. They specifically want to see:

- where tenant traffic is pinned (NIC/VLAN level) vs. logical tenancy,
- how egress is inspected/controlled for Private (VPC) and Dedicated clusters,
- the exact touch-points for the control plane (management APIs, agent heartbeats) and how those are isolated, and
- a short runbook describing how we respond to tenant eviction/compromise — basically isolation + containment triggers.

Can you send an annotated asset we can attach to our SIG/SOC2 packet? Even a single-page diagram plus a short table of evidence items will do.

Appreciate it — Oliver

Oliver Grant
Head of Cloud Security, Argus Financial

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@argusfin.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-19T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: need isolation proof for Dedicated + Private deployments

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've attached an annotated diagram (argus-isolation-annotated-v1.png) and a short runbook (edge-anchor-runbook.pdf) that call out the enforcement layers. Highlights:

- Edge anchors: lightweight edge proxies terminate customer ingress and enforce per-tenant routing. For Private deployments these run in the customer VPC as managed proxies; for Dedicated they're colocated in the dedicated subnet with strict security-group rules.
- Control plane separation: management APIs use a dedicated management subnet and TLS-mutual auth for agent heartbeats; control-plane egress is whitelisted and routable only to our management endpoints.
- Egress inspection: for Private we support VPC peering or PrivateLink to route egress to the customer's inspection appliances; for Dedicated we provide an egress eBPF hop that emits metadata to SIEM and optionally mirrors traffic to an inspection endpoint.
- Tenant evacuation: the runbook shows stepwise actions — isolate datastore mounts, revoke tenant API keys, suspend traffic at the edge anchor, snapshot KV caches, and if needed advertise BGP blackhole for that tenant range.

Attached files: argus-isolation-annotated-v1.png (single-page), control-plane-egress-matrix.xlsx (evidence table), edge-anchor-runbook.pdf (procedural steps).

Two quick asks: (1) Are you ok with us redacting specific IPs from the diagram for the public SOC packet? (2) Do you want a short text table mapping each diagram item to SIG/SOC2 evidence IDs (I can add those in the spreadsheet if helpful)?

-Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Architect, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@argusfin.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: need isolation proof for Dedicated + Private deployments

Adding a few technical clarifications for the artifact so Argus security can map controls to evidence. I pasted the minimal table below and updated the workbook column names (see control-plane-egress-matrix.xlsx).

- Enforcement layers (diagram labels):
  * L1 Edge Anchor (ingress termination): per-tenant TLS SNI + mTLS to upstream; enforces routing and rate limits. Evidence: edge-anchor-runbook.pdf step 3; TLS cert inventory.
  * L2 Network Fence (VLAN/SG): For Dedicated we assign tenant VLANs with inter-VLAN ACLs. Evidence: VLAN assignment logs, provisioning script hashes. For Private, we rely on customer VPC security groups + explicit route tables; Evidence: VPC peering config + terraform plan.
  * L3 Host/Process (container/VM): kernel seccomp profiles, process cgroups and namespacing. Evidence: hardened AMI build id, container image SBOM.
  * L4 Data Plane Eviction (storage isolations): snapshot workflow and retained snapshot artifact ids. Evidence: snapshot-job logs, KMS key ACLs.

- Control plane connectivity: agents authenticate with mTLS to management endpoints. We rotate client certs quarterly and publish rotation logs to the audit bucket (s3://redwood-audit/rotations). Evidence: cert rotation manifest, audit log extract (redacted).

- Egress: we support three egress modes per customer: Routed via customer inspection, Routed via Redwood managed inspection cluster, or Deny-all with approved exceptions. The spreadsheet enumerates which customers are on each mode. Evidence: egress-policy ACLs + SIEM forwarder config.

- Operational play: containment timer thresholds are configurable (default 5 mins to suspend agent, 30 mins to snapshot and revoke keys). These are in the runbook and are triggered by SIEM rules. Evidence: playbook run logs.

Oliver — if you want, we can produce a redacted version of the diagrams for the public SOC packet and a full internal version for your internal review.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
